treadmill.definition: An exercise device consisting of an endless belt on which a person can walk or jog without changing place.
treadmill.exampleUsage: The treadmill was used during the activity.

stationary-bike.definition: An indoor exercise machine with pedals and a seat that simulates cycling without moving forward.
stationary-bike.exampleUsage: The stationary bike was used during a supervised fitness session.

elliptical.definition: Characterized by extreme economy of expression or omission of superfluous elements.

rowing-machine.definition: An exercise machine that simulates the pulling motion of rowing a boat.
rowing-machine.exampleUsage: The rowing machine is part of the cardio area.

stair-climber.definition: An exercise machine that simulates repeatedly climbing steps.
stair-climber.exampleUsage: The stair climber is located near the treadmills.

jump-rope.definition: A toy with a rope that is swung under the feet.

spin-bike.definition: A sturdy stationary exercise bike designed for indoor cycling classes.
spin-bike.exampleUsage: The indoor-cycling class uses spin bikes.

exercise-mat.definition: A padded mat used for floor-based exercise, stretching, or movement practice.
exercise-mat.exampleUsage: The student used an exercise mat during the supervised class.

step-platform.definition: A low raised platform used in step-based fitness exercises.
step-platform.exampleUsage: The step platform was set out for the group class.

punching-bag.definition: A padded hanging or standing bag used for supervised boxing or martial-arts training.
punching-bag.exampleUsage: The punching bag was used during a coached training session.

battle-rope.definition: A thick heavy rope used in some supervised fitness training as resistance equipment.
battle-rope.exampleUsage: Battle ropes were stored in the functional-training area.

medicine-ball.definition: A heavy, weighted ball used to build strength and improve physical fitness.

foam-roller.definition: A firm foam cylinder used for stretching, mobility work, or gentle self-massage.
foam-roller.exampleUsage: The foam roller was available in the recovery area.

yoga-mat.definition: A soft mat used during yoga exercises.

fitness-tracker.definition: A wearable device that records activity information such as steps or exercise time.
fitness-tracker.exampleUsage: The fitness tracker recorded the walk.

armband.definition: A band worn around the upper arm.

lock.definition: A device used to secure a bicycle or prevent access.

locker.definition: A small locked compartment for a student’s belongings.

shaker-bottle.definition: A bottle with a mixing insert or ball designed to blend powdered drink ingredients with liquid.
shaker-bottle.exampleUsage: The shaker bottle was washed after use.

dumbbell.definition: A short bar with a weight at each end, used for exercise.

barbell.definition: A bar to which heavy discs are attached at each end.

kettlebell.definition: A heavy exercise weight shaped like a ball with a handle on top.
kettlebell.exampleUsage: Kettlebells were stored on a low rack.

weight-bench.definition: A padded bench designed to support a person during supervised strength exercises.
weight-bench.exampleUsage: The weight bench was placed beside the rack.

pull-up-bar.definition: A horizontal bar designed to support body-weight pulling exercises.
pull-up-bar.exampleUsage: The pull-up bar is fixed securely to the frame.

leg-press.definition: A strength-training machine in which the user pushes a weighted platform with the legs.
leg-press.exampleUsage: The leg-press machine is in the strength area.

cable-machine.definition: A resistance-training machine that uses adjustable cables, pulleys, and weight stacks.
cable-machine.exampleUsage: The cable machine has several adjustable attachments.

smith-machine.definition: A strength-training machine with a barbell guided along fixed rails.
smith-machine.exampleUsage: The Smith machine guides the bar along vertical rails.

squat-rack.definition: A sturdy frame designed to support a barbell at adjustable heights during supervised strength training.
squat-rack.exampleUsage: The squat rack was checked by gym staff.

resistance-band.definition: An elastic band that provides increasing resistance when stretched.
resistance-band.exampleUsage: Resistance bands were stored by size.

weight-plate.definition: A flat circular weight designed to be placed on a barbell or compatible exercise machine.
weight-plate.exampleUsage: Weight plates were returned to the storage rack.

weight-belt.definition: A supportive belt used in some strength-training settings; it does not replace proper coaching or technique.
weight-belt.exampleUsage: The trainer explained that a weight belt is specialized equipment, not a substitute for instruction.

wrist-wraps.definition: Fabric supports wrapped around the wrists during some strength or sports activities.
wrist-wraps.exampleUsage: Wrist wraps were stored with other training accessories.

knee-sleeves.definition: Close-fitting elastic sleeves worn around the knees for warmth or light support during some activities.
knee-sleeves.exampleUsage: The athlete wore knee sleeves during supervised training.

chalk.definition: To write, draw, or trace with chalk.

gym-towel.definition: A small towel used to dry sweat or wipe personal equipment during exercise.
gym-towel.exampleUsage: She carried a clean gym towel.

water-bottle.definition: A container used for carrying drinking water.

protein-powder.definition: A powdered food or dietary supplement containing concentrated protein; teenagers should not use supplements to chase body ideals and should discuss dietary needs with a parent or qualified health professional.
protein-powder.exampleUsage: The nutrition lesson treats protein powder as a supplement, not a requirement for fitness.

sneakers.definition: A canvas shoe with a pliable rubber sole.

sports-bra.definition: A supportive bra designed to reduce breast movement during physical activity.
sports-bra.exampleUsage: The sportswear section includes different sports-bra designs.

tank-top.definition: A close-fitting sleeveless shirt has broad shoulder straps, a low neckline, and no opening down the front. It is often worn over a shirt or blouse.

shorts.definition: (used in the plural) trousers that end at or above the knee.

leggings.definition: A garment covering the leg (usually extending from the knee to the ankle).
leggings.exampleUsage: The glossary uses the term "Leggings" in an educational description.

sweatband.definition: A band of material tied around the forehead or wrist to absorb sweat.

athletic-socks.definition: Socks designed for sports or exercise, often with cushioning or moisture-managing fabric.
athletic-socks.exampleUsage: She wore athletic socks with training shoes.

hoodie.definition: A casual sweatshirt made from cotton or fleece, with a drawstring hood and a front pocket.

gym-gloves.definition: Gloves designed to protect the hands or improve comfort during some gym activities.
gym-gloves.exampleUsage: Gym gloves were stored in the training bag.

wrist-wrap.definition: A fabric support wrapped around one wrist during some strength or sports activities.
wrist-wrap.exampleUsage: A wrist wrap was listed among the gym accessories.

gym-bag.definition: A bag used to carry exercise clothing, shoes, towels, and other personal items.
gym-bag.exampleUsage: His gym bag contained shoes and a towel.

headband.definition: A band worn around or over the head.

sports-watch.definition: A wristwatch designed with features for exercise or outdoor activity, such as timers or activity tracking.
sports-watch.exampleUsage: The sports watch recorded the session duration.

athletic-shoes.definition: Shoes designed to support movement during sport or exercise.
athletic-shoes.exampleUsage: She wore athletic shoes appropriate for the class.

track-pants.definition: Comfortable athletic trousers, often made from lightweight or stretchy fabric.
track-pants.exampleUsage: He changed into track pants before practice.

base-layers.definition: Close-fitting clothing worn next to the skin beneath other layers to manage warmth or moisture.
base-layers.exampleUsage: The runner wore light base layers in cool weather.

jacket.definition: A short outer garment worn over other clothes.

towel.definition: A piece of absorbent cloth used for drying your body or other things.

push-up.definition: A body-weight exercise in which the body is raised and lowered using the arms while kept generally straight.
push-up.exampleUsage: The coach included push-ups in a supervised fitness circuit.

squat.definition: To perform the squat weightlifting exercise.

lunge.definition: (fencing) an attacking thrust made with one foot forward and the back leg straight and with the sword arm outstretched forward.

plank.definition: An endorsed policy in the platform of a political party.

deadlift.definition: A weight training exercise in which a loaded barbell is lifted off the ground to the hips, then lowered back to the ground.

bench-press.definition: A strength exercise performed face up on a bench while pressing weights upward.

sit-up.definition: A floor exercise in which the upper body is raised from a lying position toward the knees.
sit-up.exampleUsage: The class included sit-ups as one optional exercise.

burpee.definition: A vigorous body-weight exercise combining a squat-like movement, a plank position, and returning to standing.
burpee.exampleUsage: Burpees appeared in the supervised conditioning class.

pull-up.definition: A body-weight exercise in which a person pulls the body upward while holding an overhead bar.
pull-up.exampleUsage: The trainer demonstrated a pull-up during the supervised session.

jumping-jack.definition: A toy figure with hinged joints can be made to dance by pulling attached strings.

speed-bag.definition: A small suspended punching bag designed to rebound quickly during boxing training.
speed-bag.exampleUsage: The speed bag was used only in the coached boxing area.

repetition.definition: One complete performance of an exercise movement.

set.definition: Several exercises intended to be done in series.

circuit-training.definition: A workout format that moves through a series of different exercise stations or activities.
circuit-training.exampleUsage: The class used circuit training with supervised stations.

hiit.definition: High-intensity interval training, a workout format alternating short hard-effort periods with recovery periods.
hiit.exampleUsage: The gym describes HIIT as a demanding class that should be matched to a person's fitness and supervision needs.

cross-training.definition: Training that uses different types of exercise or sport to develop varied fitness skills and reduce repetitive load.
cross-training.exampleUsage: The school program uses cross-training rather than only one activity.

warm-up.definition: A brief activity before a demanding task or performance prepares the body and mind for what follows.

cool-down.definition: A period of lighter activity after exercise intended to gradually reduce effort.
cool-down.exampleUsage: The coached class ended with a short cool-down.

locker-room.definition: A room in a sports facility or workplace where people change clothes and leave personal belongings in lockers.

shower.definition: A place or device that sprays water over you so you can wash your body.
shower.exampleUsage: The shower was used during the activity.

sauna.definition: A heated room in which people sit to sweat and relax.

swimming-pool.definition: A large basin filled with water where people swim, practice, relax, or compete.

juice-bar.definition: A counter or shop that sells fruit or vegetable juices and other non-alcoholic drinks.
juice-bar.exampleUsage: The gym's juice bar sells fruit drinks.

reception-desk.definition: A staffed area in an office, hotel, institution, or support service where visitors and callers are welcomed, identified, and sent to the right person or service.

mirror-wall.definition: A wall covered with large mirrors, often used in studios or gyms to observe movement.
mirror-wall.exampleUsage: The fitness studio has a mirror wall.

steam-room.definition: A heated room designed for bathing in steam; in Britain, it is also called a vapour bath.

personal-trainer.definition: A fitness professional who provides individualized exercise instruction and supervision within their qualifications.
personal-trainer.exampleUsage: The personal trainer adjusted the session for the client's current ability.

spotter.definition: A person employed to keep watch for some anticipated event.

exercise-ball.definition: A large inflatable ball used in supervised fitness, balance, or rehabilitation exercises.
exercise-ball.exampleUsage: The exercise ball was stored in the studio.

stretch.definition: A large and unbroken expanse or distance.
